cases.n: Rotherham — Jay inquiry (1,400 children, 1997–2013)
cases.who: Group-based exploitation networks; Rotherham Metropolitan Borough Council; South Yorkshire Police
cases.cover: Three earlier reports (2002, 2003, 2013) on exploitation were effectively suppressed or ignored; police did not treat the abuse as a priority.
cases.d: Professor Alexis Jay's independent inquiry, published 26 August 2014, estimated that about 1,400 children were sexually exploited in Rotherham between 1997 and 2013, some as young as 11. It described the collective failures of the council and South Yorkshire Police as 'blatant'. The report said most known perpetrators were of Pakistani heritage, and that frontline staff were confused about what might be seen as racist. The council leader resigned within hours of publication.
cases.cite: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Exploitation in Rotherham 1997–2013 (Alexis Jay), 26 August 2014; Al Jazeera, 26 Aug 2014

cases.n: Operation Stovewood — NCA Rotherham investigation
cases.victims_note: potential victims identified by the NCA
cases.who: National Crime Agency investigation into non-recent exploitation in Rotherham
cases.d: The National Crime Agency took over the Rotherham investigation in 2014. Its page reports about 1,150 potential victims identified, more than 220 people arrested or interviewed voluntarily, and 39 people convicted with about 470 years of prison sentences. On 8 August 2025 the NCA agreed to take over an investigation, directed by the Independent Office for Police Conduct, into allegations of child sexual abuse by former South Yorkshire Police officers (allegations; no finding yet).
cases.cite: National Crime Agency, Operation Stovewood page and statement of 8 August 2025

cases.n: Rochdale — Operation Span convictions and 2024 review
cases.who: Grooming network linked to two takeaway restaurants; Greater Manchester Police; Rochdale Council
cases.cover: Police identified ring-leaders in 2007 but did not pursue them; Operation Span launched over two years after the first reports.
cases.d: In May 2012 nine men were convicted after Operation Span, which Greater Manchester Police began in December 2010, more than two years after it was first told of abuse linked to two takeaways. Girls as young as 12 were plied with drink and drugs and passed between men for cash. A 173-page review published 15 January 2024 found children were 'left at the mercy' of gangs between 2004 and 2013 through a 'lamentable strategic failure' of senior police and council leaders; it identified hundreds of potential victims, mainly white girls from poor backgrounds, abused by Asian men, and said 96 men were still a potential risk to children.
cases.cite: Greater Manchester Combined Authority, Operation Span review (Spicer/Woodhouse), January 2024; ITV News, 15 Jan 2024

cases.n: Oxford — Operation Bullfinch and 2015 Serious Case Review
cases.victims_note: Serious Case Review estimate: more than 350, possibly 373, over 16 years
cases.who: Grooming network; Thames Valley Police; Oxfordshire County Council
cases.d: Seven men were jailed in May 2013 for a combined minimum of 95 years after Operation Bullfinch; the trial judge said police and social services missed tell-tale signs. The Oxfordshire Serious Case Review, published 3 March 2015, estimated that more than 350 young people were sexually exploited in the county from 1999 to 2014. It found police did not believe the girls and treated them as if they had chosen their situation, and social services knew of grooming but failed to protect them. Both the police and council apologised.
cases.cite: Oxfordshire Safeguarding Children Board Serious Case Review (Bullfinch), March 2015; Public Sector Executive, 2 March 2015

cases.n: Telford — Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Exploitation
cases.victims_note: 'more than 1,000' children over at least 30 years
cases.who: Group-based exploitation networks; West Mercia Police; Telford & Wrekin Council
cases.cover: Concerns raised by officers, youth workers and teachers in the 1990s were not taken seriously; specialist CSE teams were cut to near zero after Operation Chalice.
cases.d: The inquiry chaired by Tom Crowther QC, published 12 July 2022, found more than 1,000 children were sexually exploited in Telford over at least 30 years. Agencies dismissed the abuse as 'child prostitution', blamed children for 'lifestyle choices', and failed to investigate partly from nervousness about race. Seven men were jailed in 2013 after Operation Chalice. West Mercia Police and the council apologised; the inquiry found no evidence of corruption.
cases.cite: Independent Inquiry Telford Child Sexual Exploitation (Tom Crowther QC), 12 July 2022; ITV News, 12 Jul 2022

cases.n: Newcastle — Operation Sanctuary
cases.victims_note: about 700 across the Northumbria Police area, 108 in Newcastle (Joint Serious Case Review)
cases.who: Grooming networks; Northumbria Police
cases.d: Operation Sanctuary began in 2014 and led to 18 people being jailed for sexually abusing girls and young women they had groomed in Newcastle. The Joint Serious Case Review, published 23 February 2018, put the number of victims at about 700 across the Northumbria area, 108 of them in Newcastle. It found no evidence that concerns about political correctness or accusations of racism made police reluctant to investigate, and called for law changes on sexual exploitation.
cases.cite: Newcastle Safeguarding Children Board, Joint Serious Case Review concerning sexual exploitation (David Spicer), February 2018; Euronews, 23 Feb 2018

cases.n: Huddersfield — Operation Tendersea
cases.who: Grooming networks; West Yorkshire Police investigation
cases.d: In October 2018, 20 men were convicted at Leeds Crown Court of abusing girls as young as 11 in Huddersfield between 2004 and 2011; the ringleader's convictions involved 11 girls. By April 2023 Operation Tendersea had convicted 42 men in several trials for abuse between 1995 and 2013, with 505 years and six months of sentences.
cases.cite: ITV News, 19 Oct 2018; Pocklington Post/Yorkshire Post, April 2023

cases.n: Derby — Operation Retriever
cases.who: Grooming network; Derbyshire Police investigation
cases.d: Derbyshire Police's Operation Retriever led to the conviction of nine men in 2010 for grooming and sexually abusing 26 girls, one aged 12. Thirteen men had been charged and eleven stood trial.
cases.cite: Heart East Midlands, 2010; BBC News 'Derby sex gang convicted of grooming and abusing girls', 24 Nov 2010

cases.n: Halifax/Calderdale — West Yorkshire grooming trials
cases.who: Grooming networks; West Yorkshire Police
cases.d: On 6 November 2024, 20 men were jailed for more than 200 years combined for raping and abusing four girls aged 12 to 16 in Calderdale between 2001 and 2010, after three West Yorkshire Police investigations. In May 2026 six more men were convicted over the abuse of one girl from 2006 to 2009, which she reported to police in 2019.
cases.cite: ITV Calendar, 6 Nov 2024; Crown Prosecution Service, May 2026

cases.n: Keighley — 2016 convictions
cases.who: Grooming network
cases.d: In February 2016 twelve men were jailed, with sentences of up to 20 years, for sexually exploiting a vulnerable teenage girl in Keighley. A further six men were jailed in 2022 for the systematic rape of another teenage girl in the town.
cases.cite: BBC News 'Keighley abuse: Twelve men jailed for sexually exploiting girl', 8 Feb 2016; Yorkshire Evening Post 2022

cases.n: Oldham — 2022 assurance review
cases.who: Oldham Council; Greater Manchester Police; shisha bars, residential homes and taxis
cases.d: The review published 20 June 2022 found 'serious failings' by Oldham Council and Greater Manchester Police: police and council knew of risks from shisha bars by late 2010 yet children of 13 and 14 still visited them in 2013, and multi-agency child-protection procedures were often not started. It criticised how a former council welfare rights officer, later convicted of rape and trafficking, was investigated. The review found no evidence of a cover-up by senior managers or councillors. Oldham is the first confirmed area for local investigation under the 2025 national inquiry.
cases.cite: Greater Manchester Combined Authority, Review into historic safeguarding practices in Oldham, June 2022

cases.n: Casey national audit on group-based child sexual exploitation
cases.who: Home Office; police forces in England and Wales
cases.d: Baroness Casey's audit, published 16 June 2025, found that data flaws meant the scale of group-based exploitation could not be assessed, and that perpetrator ethnicity was not recorded for about two-thirds of cases. Local data from three police force areas showed 'disproportionate numbers of men from Asian ethnic backgrounds amongst suspects', which she said warranted further examination; she said flawed data had been used to dismiss concerns. The government accepted all 12 recommendations, including mandatory ethnicity and nationality data for suspects, charging adult sex with under-16s as rape, an NCA-led national operation, and a national inquiry with statutory powers.
cases.cite: National Audit on Group-based Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (Baroness Casey), 16 June 2025

cases.n: Home Office paper on group-based CSE characteristics (2020)
cases.who: Home Office
cases.d: The Home Office paper published 15 December 2020 reviewed the evidence on group-based child sexual exploitation. It said research found group-based offenders were 'most commonly White' and that available data did not support conclusions that any one ethnic group was over-represented, while stressing that data were poor and inconsistently recorded. The Home Secretary's foreword said community and cultural factors were 'clearly relevant'. The 2025 Casey audit later said such flawed data had been used to dismiss concerns.
cases.cite: Home Office, Group-based child sexual exploitation: characteristics of offending, 15 Dec 2020; UCL analysis, Dec 2020

cases.n: Independent Inquiry into Grooming Gangs (2025–)
cases.who: National panel overseeing local investigations
cases.d: On 9 December 2025 the Home Secretary named Baroness Anne Longfield, former Children's Commissioner, as chair of a national inquiry with full statutory powers overseeing local investigations into grooming gangs, following Casey's recommendation. It is time-limited to three years with a £65m budget, will hold individuals and institutions to account, and Oldham is the first confirmed local investigation. Final terms of reference were due by March 2026.
cases.cite: Local Government Lawyer, 9 Dec 2025; GOV.UK Independent inquiry into grooming gangs collection

cases.n: Backpage.com — seizure, CEO plea and owners' convictions
cases.who: Backpage.com classified advertising website
cases.d: US authorities seized Backpage.com in April 2018. On 12 April 2018 CEO Carl Ferrer pleaded guilty to conspiracy to facilitate prostitution and money laundering; the Justice Department said the site earned hundreds of millions of dollars from 'escort' ads and that traffickers used it to advertise children and adults alike. In November 2023 a Phoenix jury convicted co-owners Scott Spear and John Brunst on Travel Act and money-laundering counts and Michael Lacey on one count of international concealment money laundering; co-founder James Larkin died on 31 July 2023 before trial. On 28 August 2024 Spear and Brunst were sentenced to 10 years and Lacey to five; DOJ said the scheme earned more than $500 million.
cases.cite: US Department of Justice press releases, 12 April 2018 and 28 August 2024

cases.n: Craigslist adult services closure (2010)
cases.who: Craigslist
cases.d: In September 2010 Craigslist removed its 'adult services' section from its US site, replacing it with a 'censored' label, after a letter from 18 state attorneys general led by Connecticut's Richard Blumenthal. The letter said the section carried rampant prostitution ads and facilitated human trafficking, including ads involving children. Blumenthal estimated the section could generate over $36 million in revenue. Much of the advertising later moved to Backpage, which AGs urged to close its own section that month.
cases.cite: JURIST, Sept 2010; Illinois Attorney General, 21 Sept 2010
cases.url2: https://illinoisattorneygeneral.gov/News-Room/2006-2018-Press-Archive/201009-21 URGES BACKPAGEdotCOM TO REMOVE ADULT SERVICES SECTION.pdf

cases.n: Pornhub/MindGeek (Aylo) — card cut-off, DOJ agreement and FTC/Utah settlement
cases.place: Brooklyn, New York (EDNY); Salt Lake City (FTC/Utah)
cases.who: Aylo Holdings (formerly MindGeek), owner of Pornhub
cases.d: After a New York Times column by Nicholas Kristof on 4 December 2020 reported child sexual abuse material and non-consensual videos on Pornhub, the site banned uploads from unverified users and Mastercard (10 Dec 2020) and Visa stopped card acceptance. On 21 December 2023 Aylo entered a deferred prosecution agreement in Brooklyn over unlawful monetary transactions involving sex-trafficking proceeds (linked to GirlsDoPorn, whose victims were adult women), paying over $1.8 million plus victim compensation and accepting a three-year monitor; Aylo did not plead guilty. On 3 September 2025 Aylo agreed to pay $5 million to the FTC and Utah, which alleged it knowingly profited from child sexual abuse material and that its fingerprinting system was ineffective from at least 2017 to August 2021.
cases.cite: TechSpot 11 Dec 2020; AP via WOWT 22 Dec 2023; TechCrunch 3 Sept 2025 (FTC and Utah Division of Consumer Protection settlement)

cases.n: FBI Operation Cross Country XIII (2023)
cases.victims_note: 59 minor victims of child sex trafficking/exploitation identified or located; 200 victims in total
cases.who: FBI and partner agencies
cases.d: During a two-week operation in July 2023, announced 1 August 2023, the FBI and partners identified and located 200 sex-trafficking victims, including 59 minor victims of child sex trafficking and sexual exploitation, and located 59 actively missing children. 68 trafficking suspects and 126 suspects of child sexual exploitation and trafficking offences were identified or arrested.
cases.cite: US Department of Justice, 'Operation Cross Country XIII', 1 Aug 2023

cases.n: Carreto family — Tenancingo to New York trafficking
cases.who: Carreto family pimping network based in Tenancingo, Tlaxcala
cases.d: From 1991 to 2004 the Carreto family, based in San Miguel de Tenancingo, Tlaxcala, recruited young, poor women and girls in Mexico by deception and forced them into prostitution in brothels in Queens and Brooklyn, using rape, threats and forced abortion. Josue and Gerardo Flores Carreto were sentenced to 50 years each in April 2006 and Daniel Perez Alonso to 25 years. Their mother Consuelo Carreto Valencia was extradited in January 2007 and pleaded guilty to sex trafficking on 22 July 2008.
cases.cite: US Department of Justice press release, 22 July 2008; UNODC SHERLOC, United States v. Carreto et al.

cases.n: Rendon-Reyes trafficking organization (Tenancingo)
cases.victims_note: at least 8 victims named in five sentencings, including one minor
cases.who: Rendon-Reyes Trafficking Organization, Tenancingo, Tlaxcala
cases.d: From December 2004 to November 2015 the Tenancingo-based Rendon-Reyes organization smuggled women and girls from Mexico and Central America into the US, forced them into prostitution and laundered proceeds back to Mexico. In January 2019 five members were sentenced in Brooklyn to between 15 and 25 years; others had pleaded guilty to racketeering and sex trafficking.
cases.cite: US Attorney's Office EDNY press release, 7 January 2019

cases.n: Marita Verón case — Tucumán brothel network
cases.who: Brothel and trafficking ring in Tucumán province
cases.cover: Campaigners and the victim's family's lawyers said police were often paid to protect prostitution rings; trial court acquitted all 13 in 2012.
cases.d: Marita Verón, aged 23, disappeared in Tucumán in 2002, allegedly abducted into forced prostitution. In December 2012 a Tucumán court acquitted all 13 defendants, provoking national protests and calls to impeach the judges. In December 2013 Tucumán's Supreme Court reversed the acquittals and found 10 of the 13 guilty. Her mother's foundation, created in 2008, says it has helped free hundreds of women and girls from brothels. (Verón was an adult; the case is included because it exposed the national network that also trafficked minors.)
cases.cite: Al Jazeera, 13 Dec 2012; AP via Fox News, 17 Dec 2013

cases.n: Netherlands — National Rapporteur estimate of exploited Dutch girls
cases.victims_note: at least 1,320 Dutch girls aged 12–17 per year (estimate, 2012–2016 data)
cases.who: Domestic pimps and 'loverboy' recruiters
cases.d: A report by National Rapporteur Corinne Dettmeijer, prepared with UNODC and published 18 October 2017, estimated that at least 1,320 underage Dutch girls aged 12 to 17 fall victim to sexual exploitation in the Netherlands each year, using 2012–2016 data. Underage girls made up nearly half of female victims in the Dutch sex industry. In October 2025 the current rapporteur reported reported exploitation cases rising from 868 (2023) to 944 (2024), with more teenage victims.
cases.cite: National Rapporteur on Trafficking in Human Beings and Sexual Violence against Children, report of 18 Oct 2017 (Reuters via Arab News); DutchNews 17 Oct 2025

cases.n: Canada — police-reported trafficking 2013–2023 (Ontario hub)
cases.victims_note: about 23% of 3,558 police-reported victims were under 18
cases.who: Mostly domestic traffickers known to victims
cases.d: Statistics Canada reported on 1 November 2024 that police recorded 4,543 trafficking incidents from 2013 to 2023; about 23% of 3,558 victims were under 18 and 93% were women and girls. Ontario accounted for roughly two-thirds of incidents and Toronto alone for 20%. 91% of victims knew their trafficker and 34% were trafficked by an intimate partner; only 10% of completed adult court cases with a trafficking charge ended in a guilty decision.
cases.cite: Statistics Canada, The Daily, 'Trafficking in persons in Canada, 2023', 1 Nov 2024

cases.n: Melbourne flight attendant jailed for abusing 26 girls in the Philippines
cases.who: Australian travelling offender (airline flight attendant)
cases.d: On 30 March 2020 a 52-year-old Melbourne flight attendant was sentenced in Australia to 18.5 years' imprisonment (14 years non-parole) for sexually abusing 26 girls aged 12 to 17 in the Philippines on 25 occasions between 2010 and 2017. He was prosecuted in Australia under Commonwealth laws covering child sexual offences committed overseas.
cases.cite: Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions / AFP joint media release, 30 March 2020

cases.n: Sydney man sentenced after rescue of three children in the Philippines
cases.who: Australian offender abusing children in the Philippines
cases.d: A 64-year-old Sydney man was sentenced on 3 December 2021 to eight years and 10 months for sexual activity with children under 16 outside Australia and producing child abuse material overseas, among other charges. The AFP investigation led to three children being removed from harm in the Philippines in May 2020.
cases.cite: Australian Federal Police media release, 4 Dec 2021

cases.n: Sydney man jailed for persistent abuse of a child in the Philippines
cases.who: Australian offender procuring a child in the Philippines
cases.d: On 17 December 2021 a Sydney man was sentenced to nine years and one month for procuring a child to engage in sexual activity outside Australia and persistent sexual abuse of a child outside Australia, plus abuse-material offences. One child was rescued in the Philippines.
cases.cite: Australian Federal Police media release, 17 Dec 2021

cases.n: Brisbane man jailed for abusing children in the Visayas, Philippines
cases.who: Australian offender abusing children in the Philippines
cases.d: A 57-year-old Brisbane man was sentenced on 31 January 2022 to eight years' imprisonment (four non-parole) for abusing children overseas. Five children were rescued in the Visayas region of the Philippines in December 2019 as a result of the investigation.
cases.cite: Australian Federal Police media release, 1 Feb 2022

cases.n: Australia — passport ban for registered child sex offenders (2017)
cases.who: Australian Government
cases.d: Laws taking effect on 13 December 2017 allow Australia to cancel the passports of up to 20,000 registered child sex offenders to stop them travelling to abuse children. The Foreign Minister said about 800 registered offenders travelled overseas in 2016, often to developing countries in Asia, and about 40% did so without notifying police. Reporting at the time said about half of the trips were to Southeast Asia.
cases.cite: Jakarta Post, 13 Dec 2017; WGBH/NPR, 30 May 2017

cases.n: Philippines blacklists Australian sex offender after AFP warning (2013)
cases.who: Philippine Bureau of Immigration; Australian Federal Police
cases.d: In April 2013 Philippine immigration officers at Manila airport intercepted and blacklisted an Australian convicted in Perth in 2010 of indecent assault on children, travelling on a New Zealand passport and planning to stay in Iloilo, after an Australian police warning that he posed a risk to Filipino children. It is an example of offender travel notifications between countries.
cases.cite: Philippine Daily Inquirer (Global Nation), 26 April 2013

nets.reach_note: Backpage ran city sites in many countries, but only US prosecutions were verified here.
nets.d: Online classified site whose 'adult' and 'escort' ads were used by traffickers to sell children and adults. Seized April 2018; CEO pleaded guilty; owners convicted 2023 and sentenced 2024.

Owner of Pornhub. Lost card payments in December 2020 after reports of child abuse material; entered a 2023 US deferred prosecution agreement over sex-trafficking proceeds (GirlsDoPorn) and a 2025 FTC/Utah settlement over child abuse material.

nets.reach_note: Rendon-Reyes case documents Central American victims smuggled via Mexico; Central American recruitment sites not separately documented here.
nets.d: Family-based pimping networks from Tenancingo, Tlaxcala, that recruited Mexican and Central American women and girls by deception and forced them into prostitution in New York and other US cities. Several were prosecuted in Brooklyn (Carreto family, 2005–2008; Rendon-Reyes organization, 2019).

flows.d: Women and girls recruited in Mexico by deception and smuggled to brothels in Queens and Brooklyn; proceeds sent back to Tlaxcala.

The Rendon-Reyes organization smuggled women and girls from Mexico and Central America into the US for forced prostitution. Origin shown at Honduras for display; the DOJ release says 'Central America' without naming countries.
Several Australian men have been convicted in Australia for abusing children in the Philippines, including a flight attendant who abused 26 girls from 2010 to 2017.

flows.n: Australia → Southeast Asia registered offenders' travel
flows.size_note: about 800 registered child sex offenders travelled overseas in 2016; reporting said about half went to Southeast Asia (destination point is a regional placeholder, not Thailand specifically)
flows.d: Australia's Foreign Minister said about 800 registered child sex offenders travelled abroad in 2016, often to developing countries in Asia, with 40% not notifying police.
